11.
EXPANSION OF THE EATON FIRE REBUILD PERMIT FEE
WAIVER PROGRAM TO INCLUDE PERMIT FEES FOR REPAIRS TO ELIGIBLE STANDING
HOMES RELATED TO SMOKE, SOOT,
ASH OR WATER DAMAGE (Planning Dept.)
Recommendation :
It is recommended that the City Council:
(1)
Find that
the recommended fee reductions are exempt from the California Environmental
Quality Act (“CEQA”) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines under the “Common Sense”
exemption per Section
15061(b)(3). This exemption applies because the action involves only the waiver
of City plan check and permit fees for eligible fire‑related repairs and does
not
authorize any physical
construction activity beyond what previously existed;
(2)
Adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 General Fee Schedule to
reduce or waive various Plan Check and Permit Fees for repairing eligible
standing homes
damaged in the Eaton Fire;
(3)
Direct the City Attorney to prepare within 30 days an ordinance to amend Title 4
of the Pasadena Municipal Code (PMC) to exempt qualified repairs of eligible
residential
structures damaged by the Eaton
Fire from the City’s fees for Construction Tax; and
(4)
Direct staff to include the fees in the same
recovery efforts being done for the existing program.
Recommendation of the Economic Development
& Technology Commission :
On June 16, 2026, the Economic Development &
Technology Committee (EDTech) recommended the
City Council approve the
proposed expansion of the fee reductions for standing homes with documented
damage from the Eaton Fire as follows:
1.
Waive plan check and building permit fees collected into the Building Fund (204)
and the General Fund (101)
with a total estimated cost of $100,000 .
The reductions outlined above would apply to projects
that meet all of the following (eligible sites):
1.
Located Within a Mandatory Evacuation Order or Evacuation Warning: Area
Eligibility would extend to standing homes within officially designated
evacuation zones.
2.
Owner‑Occupied at the Time of the Eaton Fire: The property must have been
owner‑occupied as of January 7, 2025, consistent with the existing program.
For multi-family sites, only owner-occupied units are eligible for fee waivers.
3.
Documented Fire‑Related Smoke or Ash Damage: Applicants must submit a
professional report verifying fire‑related smoke or ash damage. Examples of
acceptable documentation include:
·
Licensed contractor assessments;
·
Industrial hygienist or environmental testing reports;
·
HVAC contamination assessments;
·
Insurance adjuster findings; and
·
In
some cases, dated photos showing condition of the area to be repaired ‘before’
and ‘after’ the fire may also be accepted.
4.
Repairs Limited to Restoring Pre‑Fire Conditions: Fee waivers apply only to
repairs necessary to restore the home to its pre‑fire condition. Elective
remodels or expansions are not eligible.
Staff is supportive of the expanded program and proposed eligibility criteria
for standing homes. Standing home repairs are generally smaller in scope than
full rebuilds, requiring nominal permit fees or in some instances, such as soot
removal, no city permits for the remediation. Based on the permits analyzed for
Table 1 in the agenda report, staff anticipates average waived fees of $150 to
$2,000 per property, depending on repair type and valuation. An itemized list of
the fire repair permits is included as Attachment C (of the agenda report),
which totals just over $51,000. Staff is proposing a total program budget of
$100,000 for fee waivers for standing homes to be funded by the Building Fund.
There is no cost to the General Fund for the proposed expanded fee waivers.

  Economic Development  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:

  California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") pursuant to State

  fire-related repairs and does not authorize any physical construction

  (2) Adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 General
  Fee Schedule to reduce or waive various Plan Check and Permit

  Council Minutes  10  08/17/2026
   Fees for repairing eligible standing homes damaged in the Eaton Fire
  (Resolution No. 10207);
  (3) Direct the City Attorney to prepare within 30 days an ordinance
n  to amend Title 4 of the Pasadena Municipal Code (PMC) to exempt

  Eaton Fire from the City's fees for Construction Tax; and
  (4) Direct staff to include the fees in the same recovery efforts

  Recommendation of the Economic Development & Technoloav
  Commission: On June 16, 2026, the Economic Development &
  Technology Committee (EDTech) recommended the City Council
  approve the proposed expansion of the fee reductions for standing
  homes with documented damage from the Eaton Fire as follows:
  1. Waive plan check and building permit fees collected into the
  Building Fund (204) and the General Fund (101) with a total
  estimated cost of $100,000.
  The reductions outlined above would apply to projects that meet all
  of the following (eligible sites):
  1. Located Within a Mandatory Evacuation Order or Evacuation
  Warning: Area Eligibility would extend to standing homes
  within officially designated evacuation zones.
  2. Owner-Occupied at the Time of the Eaton Fire: The property
  must have been owner-occupied as of January 7, 2025,
  consistent with the existing program. For multi-family sites,
  only owner-occupied units are eligible for fee waivers.
  3. Documented Fire-Related Smoke or Ash Damage: Applicants
  must submit a professional report verifying fire-related smoke
  or ash damage. Examples of acceptable documentation
  include:
  Licensed contractor assessments;
  • Industrial hygienist or environmental testing reports;
  HVAC contamination assessments;
  • Insurance adjuster findings; and
  • In some cases, dated photos showing condition of the
  area to be repaired 'before' and 'after' the fire may also
  be accepted.
  4. Repairs Limited to Restoring Pre-Fire Conditions: Fee
  waivers apply only to repairs necessary to restore the home
  to its pre-fire condition. Elective remodels or expansions are
  not eligible.
  Staff is supportive of the expanded program and proposed eligibility
  criteria for standing homes. Standing home repairs are generally
  smaller in scope than full rebuilds, requiring nominal permit fees or
  in some instances, such as soot removal, no city permits for the
  remediation. Based on the permits analyzed for Table 1 in the
  agenda report, staff anticipates average waived fees of $150 to
  $2,000 per property, depending on repair type and valuation. An
  itemized list of the fire repair permits is included as Attachment C (of
  the agenda report), which totals just over $51,000. Staff is proposing

  homes to be funded by the Building Fund. There is no cost to the
  General Fund for the proposed expanded fee waivers.

  Council Minutes  12  08/17/2026
   The following individuals expressed concerns regarding the delayed
  start times of City Council meetings and requested explanations for
  recent Council Committee meeting cancellations, and/or provided
  other related comments:

  Daniel James, Pasadena resident
  Humaira, Pasadena resident

  Councilmember Lyon advocated for the City Council to discuss
  meeting start/end times and frequency of meetings at a future City
  Council meeting. He expressed support for moving the City Council
  meetings to Tuesdays on a trial basis to determine if such a change
  will result in improvements in meeting efficiency. He noted his
  preference for having City Council meetings on Thursdays.

  Vice Mayor Rivas also acknowledged the issues of the delayed City
  Council meeting start times and the difficulties of maintaining a
  quorum for committee meetings. She expressed support for
  conducting City Council meetings on Tuesdays on a trial basis,
  provided that the City Council commits to holding meetings on
  Tuesdays following a national holiday.

  Councilmember Cole expressed support for City Council meetings
  occurring on Tuesdays, noting that the change would provide
  Mondays as a regular workday for City staff to respond to City
  Council questions, and also provide an additional day of preparation
  for City Councilmembers and for members of the public to review
  agenda materials prior to the meeting. He proposed that City staff
  prepare an ordinance to make the change to Tuesdays for City
  Council consideration at the next meeting when the full City Council
  is present.

  Interim City Manager Hawkesworth stated that the proposed trial
  period for having City Council meetings on Tuesdays allows the
  public, City Council, and City staff an opportunity to adjust and to
  determine if any unintended consequences occur before making the
  permanent change.

  In response to Councilmember Jones and Lyon's preferences for
  meeting to occur on Thursdays, City Clerk Jomsky reported on the
  current City Council agenda preparation process, and also stated
  that just the Community Police Oversight Commission and
  Pasadena Rental Housing Board now use the Council Chamber for
  meetings, so the move to Tuesdays would not affect their meetings.
  hie also reported City staff will coordinate to find alternative meeting
  days and times for City Council standing committee meetings, with
  input from the Chairs of each Committee.

Council Minutes  13  08/17/2026
   Discussion ensued regarding Committees that have experienced
  significant cancellation rates and the composition of the City Council
  which includes full-time working members.

  Councilmember Masuda expressed his flexibility in having City
  Council meetings take place on Tuesdays and noted the need to
  hear input from the two absent Councilmembers before making any
  permanent changes.

  Mayor Gordo expressed support for City Council meetings occurring
  on Tuesdays, while also voicing his support for the consideration of
  Thursday meetings. He acknowledged ongoing concerns about
  Council Committee quorum and attendance issues, noting that these

  regard to late starts of the City Council meetings, he explained that
  closed sessions often involve complex legal matters and can
  sometimes run longer than anticipated.
